content: There are 12 vertices on an icosahedron. Therefore, there are $\binom{12}{3}=220$ ways to choose vertices E, H, and J. Now, note what happens when we permute E, H, and J. One-fifth of the time H remains constant, so $d(E,H)$ stays the same, while $d(H,J)$ changes, so $d(E,H) > d(H,J)$ can only happen $\frac25$ of the time, namely when H is closer to J. There's a $\frac15$ chance that H and E are being exchanged, so $d(E,H)$ and $d(H,J)$ are just interchanged. Again, $d(E,H) > d(H,J)$ can only happen $\frac25$ of the time. When H and J are exchanged, those chances are also $\frac25$. Therefore, the probability is $\frac15 \left( \frac25 + \frac25 + \frac25 \right) = \boxed{\frac13}$, so the required string is $\boxed{\text{DDDDD}}$.
